claim: Mahsuri was executed for adultery she didn't commit, bled white blood proving innocence, and cursed Langkawi with seven generations of bad luck after which it prospered.
quote: When she was stabbed, white blood flowed from the wound, signifying her innocence. With her dying breath, Mahsuri cursed Langkawi to have seven generations of bad luck.

claim: Langkawi legends: Mahsuri's seven-generation curse and the giants' brawl that named Belanga Pecah and Kuah.
quote: The broken pot gave its name to the nearby village of Belanga Pecah, and the gravy to the island's capital, Kuah.

claim: In 2000 Mahsuri's seventh-generation descendant Wan Aishah (Sirintra Yayee) was traced in Phuket and her tomb visit is said to have lifted the curse.
quote: Wan Aishah Wan Nawawi (Sirintra Yayee) is the seventh-generation descendant of the legendary Mahsuri.

claim: Kota Mahsuri complex was founded in 1983 and includes the tomb, a recreated traditional house, theatre and diorama museum.
quote: Kota Mahsuri was founded in 1983 and was one of Langkawi's first tourist attractions.

claim: Entry to the Field of Burnt Rice is free, reached through a bazaar selling batik and gamat products.
quote: To get to the rice fields, you have to go through the bazaar where there are small shops selling various items like batik, gamat. There is no charge for entering this place.

claim: During the 1821 Siamese invasion villagers burned their own rice stores, naming Padang Matsirat the field of burnt rice.
quote: Legend has it that during a Siamese invasion in 1821, the locals set fire to the rice fields to prevent the invaders from harvesting the crops.

claim: A brawl between giant clans Mat Cincang and Mat Raya spilled gravy and broke crockery, naming villages, before the gods turned the giants into mountains.
quote: In the brawl, the crockery was angrily kicked around and its gravy spilt. From the broken pieces emerged the village of Belanga Pecah.

claim: Place names Kuah (gravy), Belanga Pecah (broken pot), Kisap (seeped), Tanjung Cincin (ring) and Air Hangat (hot water) all derive from the giants' wedding brawl.
quote: The engagement ring was flung and the place where it landed became Tanjung Cincin. A cauldron of hot water was broken at Ayer Hangat, the Hot Springs.

claim: Kuah, Langkawi's capital, takes its name from the Malay word for gravy.
quote: Kuah, which means gravy in Malay.

claim: Lagenda Langkawi, a $10M open-air legend sculpture park opened 1996 in Kuah, is now abandoned and accessible via an unlocked gate.
quote: we were literally the only visitors to this huge park. Exploring the abandoned Lagenda Langkawi theme park was fun, albeit a tad creepy.

claim: Langkawi's Snake Sanctuary ceased operation in 2012 due to funding and visitor shortfalls and sits abandoned.
quote: It housed a collection of venomous and non-venomous snakes, but ceased operation in 2012 due to funding issues and lack of visitors.

claim: Black Sand Beach (Pantai Pasir Hitam) is on the northern coast about 25 km from Pantai Cenang.
quote: The small stretch of coastline along the northern shore sits approximately 25 kilometres from Pantai Cenang.

claim: The black sand is explained by legend as battle-ash and scientifically by tourmaline and ilmenite washing down from Gunung Raya granite.
quote: The black sands are caused by large amounts of tourmaline and ilmenite from the granite in Gunung Raya.

claim: Guided after-dark rainforest tours seek nocturnal wildlife including the colugo and dusky leaf monkeys.
quote: Langkawi: Nighttime Rainforest Tour with Nature Guide.

claim: The Rainforest Afterdark walk descends from Gunung Raya to Lubuk Semilang to find the Sunda colugo.
quote: As dusk settles, visitors descend from Gunung Raya towards Lubuk Semilang, the mission is to glimpse the rare sunda colugo also known as the flying lemur.

claim: Langkawi is among the best places to see the colugo, which can glide over 100 m losing only 10 m of elevation.
quote: The colugo can glide over 100 meters while only losing 10 meters of elevation. Langkawi is the best place on the planet to find the cute colugo.

claim: Three hornbill species occur in Langkawi and Gunung Raya is the only place to see all three.
quote: 3 species of hornbill can be found in Langkawi - and the only place to see all 3 is Gunung Raya.

claim: Buffalo Park lets visitors watch buffalo-milk mozzarella made, try hand-milking 9-10am, admission RM3, but is poorly signposted.
quote: Visitors can also see the live making process of Mozzarella Cheese made from buffalo milk. The admission fee for Malaysians is RM3.

claim: Buffalo Park is a dairy farm amid mountains and paddy fields in Kampung Nyior Chabang, about 20 minutes from Kuah.
quote: Buffalo Park is a dairy farm in natural surroundings of mountains and paddy fields, located in Kampung Nyior Chabang, approximately 20 minutes from Kuah town.

claim: Atma Alam Batik Art Village is the home of Langkawi's handmade batik with workshop, showroom and gallery.
quote: Atma Alam Batik Art Village in Langkawi showcases and sells exclusive and handmade batik paintings, batik dresses and handicrafts.

claim: Atma Alam in Padang Matsirat offers free entry and hands-on batik activities, about 5 km from Kuah.
quote: Admission is free, located approximately 5 km from Kuah; visitors can try the batik craft through simple, hands-on activities.

claim: Galeria Perdana, run by the Department of Museums Malaysia, displays gifts and awards given to former PM Mahathir and his wife.
quote: Galeria Perdana showcases a vast collection of gifts and awards presented to the fourth Prime Minister of Malaysia, Tun Dr. Mahathir Mohamad.

claim: Galeria Perdana's diplomatic gifts include Formula One cars and Ming vases painted with the prime minister's face.
quote: This museum displays the sort of gifts that get passed between heads of state (Formula One race cars, Ming vases painted with the prime minister's face).

claim: Air Hangat is a rare saltwater hot spring 14 km north of Kuah with three communal wells up to 42C and private jacuzzis.
quote: Visitors can dip their feet in one of 3 communal springs, ranging in temperature from cool to 42 degrees, or hire a private jacuzzi.

claim: Telaga Tujuh's seven pools are legendarily the bathing pools of fairies who left after a prince tried to capture one.
quote: The seven wells of Telaga Tujuh are bathing pools of the fairies, giving its water a mystical healing capacity.

claim: Telaga Tujuh's upper pools require a steep 600-step climb on slippery boulders with fatal-fall risk, and macaques snatch bags.
quote: The top of the waterfall is accessible by a steep climb of 600 steps. There have been cases of tourists slipping and falling from the top of the cliff, resulting in death.

claim: Tasik Dayang Bunting is a freshwater lake on Dayang Bunting island whose waters are believed to grant fertility.
quote: The grieving princess blessed the waters of the lake with the power to increase fertility of all those who swim and drink from it.

claim: The Lake of the Pregnant Maiden is a doline (collapsed limestone sinkhole) and its lore includes elves and a white crocodile.
quote: Elves, Crocodiles and Waters That Grant Fertility: The Many Wonders Of Langkawi's Tasik Dayang Bunting.

claim: Underwater World Langkawi keeps rockhopper and African penguins with daily feeding times.
quote: Animal feeding hours include African Penguin at 11:00 and 14:45 daily, and Rockhopper Penguin at 11:15 and 15:00 daily.

claim: Underwater World holds the Malaysian Book of Records for first captive rockhopper penguin breeding; tickets from about RM47.
quote: Listed in the Malaysian Book of Records for being the 1st breeding of Rockhoppers Penguins in Captivity.

claim: Art in Paradise in the Oriental Village is pitched as Malaysia's largest 3D museum with interactive optical-illusion zones.
quote: The largest 3D museum in Malaysia and the second largest in the world, spread across nine interactive zones.

claim: The 3D museum has more than 200 trompe-l'oeil artworks across nine zones and costs around RM45.
quote: 3D Art in Paradise Langkawi features more than 200 impressive artworks. It has 9 interactive sections.

claim: Eagle Square's 12 m reddish-brown eagle statue reflects the name Langkawi from helang (eagle) and kawi (reddish-brown).
quote: Langkawi comes from helang (eagle) and kawi (reddish brown). The 12 metre statue stands in the center of a plaza overlooking Kuah Jetty.

claim: The giant Eagle Square statue is one of Langkawi's most photographed landmarks.
quote: Dataran Lang / Eagle Square in Langkawi.

claim: Maha Tower is a 138 m Kuah waterfront tower with a glass-floor sky deck.
quote: MAHA Tower, standing tall at 138 meters, the Jewel of Langkawi's Skyline.

claim: Maha Tower's level-33 sky deck has a glass floor; tickets RM39 adult including free-flow food and drink.
quote: At the Sky Deck located on level 33, you can experience the spectacular glass floor. Ticket prices are RM39 for adults, admission includes free flow food and drinks.

claim: Cenang's duty-free shops are quirky: The Zon's toilet is across an alley in a separate grubby building and Teow Soon Huat is half-grocer; prices vary widely.
quote: It's weirdly located in a different building, you have to walk outside across an alley. Teow Soon Huat is strange in that it is half duty free shop and half grocer.

claim: The Langkawi International Book Village was a project to make the island a town of books.
quote: Langkawi International Book Village.

claim: The Langkawi Book Village project was officially declared a flop with its shops closed.
quote: The langkawi Book Village is dead!

claim: Temple Tree and Bon Ton are boutique heritage resorts built from antique houses in Langkawi.
quote: Boutique heritage escape in Langkawi.

claim: The resorts comprise eight original 70-110-year-old Malay, Chinese, Indian and Eurasian houses dismantled and rebuilt; they fund the LASSie animal charity.
quote: Eight antique houses of Chinese, Malay, Indian and Eurasian origin, ranging from 70 to 110 years old. The houses were dismantled and rebuilt.

claim: LASSie is a Langkawi stray-dog-and-cat shelter funded by Bon Ton/Temple Tree, receiving no government support.
quote: The LASSie Foundation does not receive support from federal, state or local governments.

claim: Langkawi became the first UNESCO Global Geopark in Southeast Asia in 2007, covering 99 islands of ancient limestone and karst.
quote: Langkawi UNESCO Global Geopark comprises all 99 islands of the archipelago, with three designated geoforest parks.

claim: Kilim's Gua Kelawar bat cave shelters about 3,000 bats with shell clusters revealing sea levels 5,000 years ago.
quote: Gua Kelawar or bat cave, home to 3,000 bats and shell clusters revealing water levels from 5,000 years ago.

claim: Langkawi Wildlife Park is billed as Asia's first fully-covered interactive park with a walk-through aviary; adult entry RM39.
quote: Asia First Fully-Covered Interactive Park. Adult: RM39.00.

claim: Laman Padi is a free open-air rice-heritage museum in Pantai Cenang with working paddy and herb gardens.
quote: Laman Padi Langkawi is an open-air museum and ecotourism site showcasing the heritage of paddy cultivation. There is typically no admission fee.

claim: In June 2026 one euro is worth roughly RM4.65.
quote: 1 EUR equals 4.65 MYR using the current mid-market exchange rate.
